title: iGaming funnels
summary: How to choose and build honest iGaming funnels: prelanders that pass review, official app installs, Telegram tipster channels with age gates and full records, retention broadcasts without pressure and bonus messaging that keeps terms clear. You finish able to measure every step and fix the one that earns the most.

lessons.title: Choosing an iGaming funnel
objectives: By the end you can name the four main iGaming funnel types and what each is good for.
You can compare funnels on cost per FTD and on value over time.
You can match a funnel to your deal type.
You can set up a fair test between two funnels.

steps.h: Why the funnel decides your cost per FTD
steps.p: The same ad, budget and offer can produce very different costs per FTD depending on what happens after the click. A funnel that warms people up can lower your cost, and one that builds a channel can keep paying for months. A badly matched funnel wastes both.

d.b: Same click, different journey, different result
d.s: Choose the funnel to fit the deal.

steps.say: Here's something that surprises beginners. The same ad, budget and offer can produce very different costs per F T D, first time deposit, depending on what happens after the click. A funnel that warms people up can lower your cost. One that builds a channel can keep paying for months. A badly matched funnel wastes both. Same click, different journey, different result. So choose the funnel to fit the deal.

steps.p: A rough guide. Each type can be done honestly or badly; the rest of this module teaches the honest version of each. Start with one type, learn it well, and add a second only when you have data.
d: Direct link|Ad straight to the operator's page
Prelander|Your page first: fixtures, preview, terms, then the operator
App install|Ad to the brand's official app in a store
Telegram channel|Ad to a channel or bot, then content and links over time
steps.say: Here are the four main types, as a rough guide. Direct link sends the ad straight to the operator's page. A prelander puts your page first, with fixtures, a preview and terms, then the operator. App install sends the ad to the brand's official app in a store. And Telegram channel sends people to a channel or bot, then content and links over time. Each can be done honestly or badly, and this module teaches the honest version. Start with one type and add a second only when you have data.

steps.p: All four end at the same place: an adult registers and deposits with a licensed operator, and the network reports it. What changes is how many steps there are, and how many chances you get to reach the person again.
steps.say: This map shows how they connect. Follow the lines from the Meta ad on the left. One goes direct to the operator sign up. One goes through a prelander. One goes through the official app. And one goes through a join request and an age gate bot. But look where they all end: an adult registers and deposits with a licensed operator, and the postback reports the F T D. What changes is the number of steps, and how many chances you get to reach the person again.

steps.h: Worked example: 1,000 clicks through each funnel
steps.p: Example. Same ad, $600 spend for 1,000 clicks at $0.60 CPC. Rates are illustrative and vary by geo and angle. The Telegram FTDs arrive over 30 days rather than on the day.
steps.more: Working. Direct: 1,000 × 12% = 120 registrations × 20% = 24 FTDs; $600 ÷ 24 = $25.00. Prelander: 1,000 × 60% = 600 clicks to the operator × 22% = 132 registrations × 22% = 29 FTDs (29.04); $600 ÷ 29 = $20.69. Telegram: 1,000 × 35% = 350 joins × 8% within 30 days = 28 FTDs; $600 ÷ 28 = $21.43. The Telegram funnel's real advantage is not in the first 30 days but in the members you can still reach next month, and the FTDs they bring later.
steps.say: Here's an example with one thousand clicks through each funnel, six hundred dollars of spend at sixty cents a click. The rates are illustrative and vary by geo and angle. Direct gives twenty four F T Ds, twenty five dollars each. The prelander gives twenty nine, about twenty dollars seventy each. Telegram gives twenty eight over thirty days, about twenty one forty three each. But Telegram's real advantage isn't in the first thirty days. It's the members you can still reach next month, and the F T Ds they bring later.

steps.h: Match the funnel to the deal
steps.p: A rough guide. CPA deals reward fast, cheap FTDs. RevShare rewards players who stay, which favours funnels where you can keep providing useful content. Treat this as a starting point, then let your own numbers decide.
steps.say: Now match the funnel to your deal, as a rough guide. On a C P A deal, cost per acquisition, you're rewarded for fast, cheap F T Ds, so a prelander or direct link fits. RevShare, revenue share, rewards players who stay, so Telegram or a prelander fits, because you keep in contact. A hybrid deal suits a prelander plus Telegram, cash now and value later. And an app only brand suits the official app. Treat this as a starting point, then let your own numbers decide.

steps.h: Ask partners what their funnels support
steps.p: Before you build, ask each partner which funnels they allow, whether they have a store-listed app for your geo and whether Telegram traffic is accepted. The answers narrow your choice.

d.note: Prefer partners who say in writing which funnel types and traffic sources they accept per geo.

steps.say: Before you build anything, ask your partners some questions. Which funnels do they allow? Do they have a store listed app for your geo? Is Telegram traffic accepted? The answers narrow your choice quickly. And prefer partners who say in writing which funnel types and traffic sources they accept for each geo.

steps.p: Follow this order. It keeps your first funnel simple and trackable, and adds complexity only when you have data and a reason. Write your choice and the reason in your log.
d: Check the deal type and allowed sources
CPA: start with a prelander
RevShare: prelander plus Telegram
App-first brand: official app only
Test one change at a time
steps.say: Here's the order for picking your first funnel. First, check the deal type and the allowed sources. If it's C P A, start with a prelander. If it's RevShare, use a prelander plus Telegram. If it's an app first brand, use the official app only. And then test one change at a time. This keeps your first funnel simple and trackable. Write your choice, and the reason, in your log.

steps.h: A fair test between two funnels
steps.p: Example. Testing a prelander against direct link for a $28 target CPA. Equal budgets, same ad, same audience, same days. Decide only when each side has spent at least 3 × target.
steps.more: Example: 3 × $28 = $84 per side. At $28 a day that is three days. Judge on projected or confirmed qualified CPA, not on clicks or registrations. If both are within 10% of each other, keep the simpler funnel; fewer steps means fewer things to break.
steps.say: Here's an example of a fair test: a prelander against a direct link, with a twenty eight dollar target C P A. Look at the table. Same ad and audience on both sides. Twenty eight dollars a day each. And a minimum spend of eighty four dollars each, that's three times target, so about three days. Decide on qualified C P A, not clicks or registrations. And if both end up within ten percent of each other, keep the simpler funnel, because fewer steps means fewer things to break.

steps.h: Lab: daily budget for a fair test
steps.p: Plan the test budget. You want each arm to reach 3 × target spend of $84 in 3 days. Work out the daily budget for one arm.

steps.p: Most funnel mistakes are about building too much too early, or comparing funnels on the wrong number. Each fix keeps your test clean, so the result you get is one you can trust and act on.

Different ads in each test arm

On the right, the fixes: one funnel, then test one alternative. Compare on qualified C P A. Judge Telegram over thirty days. And keep the same ad, audience and days. steps.h: Every funnel step carries the rules
steps.p: The 18+ line, the operator's identity, key terms and responsible gambling wording must appear wherever the user decides: ad, prelander, bot and channel. A compliant ad with a non-compliant page is a non-compliant campaign.

steps.h: Starting decision rules for funnel tests
steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. They keep tests fair and stop you from switching funnels on noise. Write them at the top of your test sheet before the test starts, not after you see the first numbers.
d: One variable per test: the funnel, nothing else
Each arm spends at least 3 × target before a decision
Telegram arms: judge at 30 days, not 3
Within 10% of each other: keep the simpler funnel
Winner must also pass the compliance gate
steps.say: Finally, some starting decision rules to adapt. One variable per test, the funnel and nothing else. Each arm spends at least three times target before a decision. Telegram arms are judged at thirty days, not three. Within ten percent of each other, keep the simpler funnel. And the winner must also pass the compliance gate. Write these at the top of your test sheet before the test starts, not after you see the first numbers.

Compare funnels on qualified CPA with equal budgets and the same ad.

lessons.title: Prelanders that pass review
objectives: By the end you can build a prelander with the six blocks an iGaming page needs.
You can work out how prelander click-through changes your cost per FTD.
You can pass click IDs and sub-IDs through the page.
You can find the weakest step in a funnel and fix it first.

steps.h: Why a prelander earns its place
steps.p: A good prelander gives people a reason to click that matches the ad, shows who the operator is and puts the terms in plain sight. That raises intent before the operator's page, which usually raises the share of FTDs. A bad one adds a step, slows the page and loses people.

d.b: Warm the click, show the terms
d.s: A prelander must add value or it only adds a step.

steps.say: Why use a prelander at all? A good one gives people a reason to click that matches the ad, shows who the operator is, and puts the terms in plain sight. That raises intent before the operator's page, which usually raises the share of F T Ds, first time deposits. A bad one just adds a step, slows the page and loses people. So warm the click and show the terms. A prelander must add value, or it only adds a step.

steps.h: The six blocks of an iGaming prelander
steps.p: Build every page from these blocks, in this order on a phone. Keep it short: one screen for the offer, one for the content. Missing any block is a reason to fix the page before you send traffic.
d: Headline that matches the ad
Real content: fixtures, odds preview, game info
Operator name and licence line
Bonus box with key terms
One clear button to the operator
Footer: 18+, gamble responsibly, help link
steps.say: Here are the six blocks, in order, on a phone. A headline that matches the ad. Real content, like fixtures, an odds preview or game info. The operator name and licence line. A bonus box with key terms. One clear button to the operator. And a footer with eighteen plus, gamble responsibly, and a help link. Keep it short, one screen for the offer and one for the content. If any block is missing, fix the page before you send traffic.

steps.p: This mock-up shows the blocks on a small screen. The terms and the 18+ marker are visible before the button, not hidden at the bottom. The content is the reason to be here.

page.p: Kick-off times and prices from a bookmaker licensed in Kenya. Welcome offer for new customers 18+: key terms below. Gamble responsibly.

steps.p: Example. $600 spend brings 1,000 visitors. Registration and FTD rates after the click stay the same. Only the prelander's click-through changes, from 55% to 65%.
steps.more: Working: 550 × 22% = 121, × 22% = 26.62 FTDs; $600 ÷ 26.62 = $22.54. 650 × 22% = 143, × 22% = 31.46; $600 ÷ 31.46 = $19.07. A ten-point rise in click-through cut CPFTD by about 15%. That is why the prelander is often the cheapest place to improve a funnel: you control it fully and can test it quickly.
steps.say: Let's see what click through is worth. In this example, six hundred dollars brings one thousand visitors, and only the prelander's click through changes, from fifty five percent to sixty five. At fifty five percent you get about twenty six and a half F T Ds, at about twenty two dollars fifty each. At sixty five percent you get about thirty one and a half, at about nineteen dollars. So a ten point rise cut the cost per F T D by about fifteen percent. The prelander is often the cheapest place to improve, because you control it fully and can test it quickly.

lessons.title: App install funnels
objectives: By the end you can tell store apps, web apps and sideloaded files apart, and why only official routes are safe.
You can calculate cost per FTD from cost per install.
You can describe how installs and deposits are tracked.

steps.h: Why app funnels can be strong, and risky
steps.p: Players who install a brand's app often come back more, because the app sits on their home screen. That can raise value per player. But app stores, platforms and laws have strict rules for real-money gambling apps, and unofficial download files are a security and policy risk.

d.s: Store-listed or the brand's own official web app.

steps.say: App funnels can be strong. Players who install a brand's app often come back more, because the app sits on their home screen, and that can raise value per player. But they're also risky. App stores, platforms and laws have strict rules for real money gambling apps, and unofficial download files are a security and policy risk. So the rule is simple: official apps only. That means store listed, or the brand's own official web app.

steps.h: Three kinds of 'app' you will be offered

steps.h: From cost per install to cost per FTD
steps.p: Each step after the install loses people. Divide the cost per install by both pass-through rates to get cost per FTD. Ask the brand for typical install-to-registration rates in your geo before you launch.
steps.more: Example. CPI $0.80. 25% of installs register, 20% of registrations deposit. $0.80 ÷ (0.25 × 0.20) = $0.80 ÷ 0.05 = $16 per FTD. If install to registration drops to 15%, CPFTD becomes $0.80 ÷ 0.03 = $26.67. Small changes in onboarding move your cost a lot.
d: CPI
(install to reg × reg to FTD)
CPFTD
steps.say: Each step after the install loses people. So to get cost per F T D, take the cost per install and divide it by both pass through rates multiplied together, install to registration and registration to F T D. For example, eighty cents per install, twenty five percent register, and twenty percent of those deposit. Eighty cents divided by zero point zero five is sixteen dollars. If registrations drop to fifteen percent, it becomes about twenty six dollars sixty seven. Small changes in onboarding move your cost a lot, so ask the brand for typical rates first.

Before you move budget, compare this with your web funnel's qualified C P A, cost per acquisition. And remember, app F T Ds also need to qualify.

objectives: By the end you can describe what separates an ethical tips channel from a harmful one.

steps.h: Why tipster channels need the strictest standards
steps.p: Tips channels sit next to people's money and hopes every day. Many channels in the market claim sure wins, sell 'fixed matches' or push people to bet more. That causes harm and attracts regulators and fraud reports. An honest channel is rarer, more trusted and lasts longer.

d.s: No guaranteed wins. No fixed matches. Adults only.

steps.say: Tips channels sit next to people's money and hopes every day. Many channels claim sure wins, sell fixed matches, or push people to bet more. That causes harm, and it attracts regulators and fraud reports. An honest channel is rarer, more trusted, and lasts longer. So the standard here is analysis, not promises. No guaranteed wins. No fixed matches. Adults only.

steps.p: Read the left column as a list of things you will never do. The right column is the standard this school teaches. If a post would fit on the left, it does not get published.

If a post would fit on the left, it doesn't get published.

steps.p: Anyone selling 'fixed matches' is either lying or describing match-fixing, which is a crime in many countries. Never post, sell, forward or hint at fixed results. If members ask, say plainly that the channel does not deal in them.

d.b: There is no such product to sell
d.s: Refuse, explain, and never hint at it.

There's no such product to sell. If members ask, say plainly that the channel doesn't deal in them. Refuse, explain, and never hint at it.

steps.h: Worked example: an honest tips record
steps.p: Example. A channel posts 120 tips in three months at average odds of 2.00, one unit each. 54 win. Publishing this honestly shows members what tipping usually looks like: even decent analysis often loses over time.
steps.more: Example maths: 54 of 120 is a 45% strike rate. At odds of 2.00 you need over 50% to break even, so the record loses 10% of stakes. Many channels hide records like this and post only winning slips. You publish the full record, pinned and updated weekly, because members deserve to see it and because it protects you from making claims you cannot support.
steps.say: Here's an example of an honest tips record. A channel posts one hundred and twenty tips in three months, at average odds of two point zero, one unit each. Fifty four win, a forty five percent strike rate. That returns one hundred and eight units, so the net is minus twelve units, minus ten percent of stakes. At those odds you'd need over fifty percent just to break even. Many channels hide records like this. You publish the full record, pinned and updated weekly, because members deserve to see it, and it stops you making claims you can't support.

steps.p: The ad brings an adult to a join request. A bot asks for age confirmation and explains what the channel is, then approves. Content, links and records follow, with opt-out at every step.

steps.h: Why retention is where RevShare is earned
steps.p: On RevShare you earn while players stay active. A channel that people keep reading brings repeat visits and new FTDs from members who were not ready on day one. But pushy broadcasts drive people away and can cause harm. The goal is useful, steady content, not volume.

steps.h: Worked example: what retention is worth
steps.p: Example. 5,000 members. Each month 2% make a first deposit through your links. You are on 35% RevShare and each FTD produces $55 NGR over three months. Compare keeping 96% of members a month with keeping 90%.
steps.more: Working: 5,000 × 0.96³ = 4,423.7, rounded 4,424; 5,000 × 0.90³ = 3,645. 2% of each gives 88 and 73 FTDs (72.9). Your share per FTD over 3 months: $55 × 35% = $19.25. 88 × $19.25 = $1,694; 73 × $19.25 = $1,405. Assumes no new joins, to isolate the effect. Every month of better retention widens the gap. Example figures only.

steps.h: Why bonus placement changes player quality
steps.p: Lead with the bonus and you often get cheap FTDs who deposit the minimum, use the bonus and leave. Lead with the product and terms and you may pay more per FTD but get players who qualify and stay. The cheapest FTD is not always the cheapest qualified FTD.
steps.say: Where you place the bonus changes player quality. Lead with the bonus, and you often get cheap F T Ds, first time deposits, who deposit the minimum, use the bonus and leave. Lead with the product and terms, and you may pay more per F T D, but you get players who qualify and stay. The cheapest F T D isn't always the cheapest qualified F T D. Cheap F T Ds can be expensive, so judge angles on true C P A.

steps.p: Example. Two angles, same offer and geo. The bonus-led angle wins on cost per FTD. The product-led angle wins on cost per qualified FTD, which is what you are paid on.
steps.more: Working: true CPA = CPFTD ÷ qualified rate. $18 ÷ 0.45 = $40.00. $24 ÷ 0.75 = $32.00. With a $40 payout, the bonus-led angle breaks even at best, while the product-led angle keeps $8 per qualified FTD. Bonus-led traffic also tends to show higher bonus cost for the operator, which can lead to quality warnings.
steps.say: Here's an example with two angles, same offer and geo. True C P A, cost per acquisition, is cost per F T D divided by the qualified rate. The bonus led angle costs eighteen dollars per F T D, but only forty five percent qualify, so true C P A is forty dollars. The product led angle costs twenty four dollars, with seventy five percent qualifying, so thirty two. With a forty dollar payout, bonus led breaks even at best, while product led keeps eight dollars per qualified F T D. Bonus led traffic can also lead to quality warnings.

steps.p: A rough guide. Mention the bonus where people decide, with its key terms beside it. Do not make it the only reason to click. Players who join for the product tend to stay.

And on the operator page, it's the brand's own, matching your wording. Mention it where people decide, but don't make it the only reason to click.

steps.h: Worked example: which fix earns most
steps.p: Example. Imagine you can lift one step's rate by 5 percentage points. Work out the extra FTDs each fix would bring with everything else unchanged. Then pick the biggest gain you can actually achieve.
steps.more: Working: base 900 × 50% = 450 × 18% = 81 × 22.2% = 18 FTDs; $600 ÷ 18 = $33.33. Views to offer at 55%: 495 × 18% = 89.1 × 22.2% = 19.8. Offer to registration at 23%: 450 × 23% = 103.5 × 22.2% = 23.0. Registration to FTD at 27.2%: 81 × 27.2% = 22.0. The same 5 points is worth most where the rate is lowest relative to its size, here offer clicks to registrations, which usually means the promise on your page does not match the operator's page.

Lift registration to F T D by five points, and you get about twenty two. So here, offer clicks to registrations wins, which usually means your page's promise doesn't match the operator's page.
